note: Pins three execution settings the bench previously left to each strategy. They change FILL and COST behaviour, so TRAIN results are no longer comparable to epoch<=3 — see comparability below. Windows, gate and slippage are carried over from epoch 3 unchanged.
changedFromPreviousEpoch: order_volume_ratio pinned to 0.05 (was unset: JQ defaults to 0.25, and only 9 of 215 held strategies set it at all)
fund order cost pinned via set_order_cost(..., type='fund') (was untouched by the override, so 170 strategies ran on their own ETF costs)
avoid_future_data pinned True (was set by only 144 of 215 strategies)

comparability.trainResultsFromEarlierEpochs: NOT comparable — a participation cap and fund costs change fills and fees. Existing rows are retained and tagged with the epoch that measured them; re-measure by screening priority rather than all at once.

rationale.orderVolumeRatio: Unset, an order can absorb an implausible share of a bar. That is the mechanism behind the two highest-scoring strategies in the library: the ETF-discount study measured sharpe falling 8.44 -> 1.10 as the volume floor rose, because the edge is constructed from the thinnest instruments. At 1,000,000 CNY, 5% of bar volume keeps a position inside what a real book could absorb.
rationale.fundOrderCost: The override patches set_commission, which does not govern type='fund'. 170 held strategies set their own fund costs, so every ETF result was running on the author's numbers rather than the bench's.
rationale.avoidFutureData: A lookahead guard left to the author means 71 of 215 strategies ran without it.
